title: I Built My AI a Leash. It Helped.

beats.text: Raise your hand if you've ever told an AI not to do something... and it did it anyway. Politely.

slides.title: I Built My AI a Leash.

beats.text: Mostly. Mostly is fine for code style. Mostly is not fine for your AWS credentials.
So I did what any reasonable engineer would do. I asked the AI to build its own leash. And it said: great idea! I've been thinking about that a lot.

slides.title: MADE BY *CLAUDE.*
slides.text: Claude, on the leash it built.

beats.text: There are three ways to influence an AI. A memory... asks nicely. A hook... says no. And a mod? A mod says no, and gives you a little badge about it.

slides.title: Three ways to influence an AI

beats.text: Here's Claude trying to read my secrets. Blocked. And honestly? It took the rejection better than most people I know.
There was a time I asked myself, every day: where am I? Which branch? Is my AWS login alive?
Now there's a band above my prompt. Yellow means AWS dies soon. Red means I'm working on a Sunday... and the rest of the world is still asleep.
I also taught it to write Slack like me. No em dashes. Ever. We don't do that here.

beats.text: While I sleep, Claude... dreams. At three a.m. it reviews its own memories and proposes changes. Proposes. Not applies. We have boundaries.
By day, I have a team. Twelve agents, one human, zero standups. I'm a manager now. I didn't apply for it.
Here's my challenge to you. Find your most annoying repeat mistake. Tell Claude: make this a hook. Ten minutes now... zero apologies later.
